## load packages

```{r load-pax-conditionally-install-if-missing, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
if(!require(compositions)) install.packages("compositions")
if(!require(robCompositions)) install.packages("robCompositions")
if(!require(car)) install.packages("car")
if(!require(MASS)) install.packages("MASS")
if(!require(vegan)) install.packages("vegan")
if(!require(flextable)) install.packages("flextable")
if(!require(randomForest)) install.packages("randomForest")
if(!require(e1071)) install.packages("e1071")
if(!require(xgboost)) install.packages("xgboost")
if(!require(viridis)) install.packages("viridis")

```

```{r load-pax, results='hide'}
library(compositions)    # log-ratio transformations (clr, alr, ilr) etc.
library(robCompositions) # imputation in log-ratio transformed compositions
library(car)             # needed for `dataEllipse` function etc.
library(MASS)            # needed for `lda` function etc.
library(vegan)           # needed for various multivariate distance methods 
library(randomForest)    # needed for random forest classification
library(e1071)           # needed for support vector machines
library(xgboost)         # needed for xgboost machine learning classification
library(viridis)         # needed for colour palettes
library(scico)           # needed for more colour palettes
library(stringr)         # needed for string manipulation
library(TeachingDemos)   # needed for `shadowtext` function
library(ggplot2)         # for plotting
library(ggspatial)       # for plotting maps
library(shadowtext)      # needed for `geom_shadowtext` function
library(plotly)          # optional for 3D plotting
library(sf)
library(terra)
```

# Make a map for checking

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
McN_nearmap <- 
  terra::rast("EPSG32750_Date20260121_Lat-32.127664_Lon116.099186_Mpp0.075_Vert.jpg")
McN_nm2 <- 
  terra::rast("EPSG32750_Date20260121_Lat-32.127015_Lon116.099343_Mpp0.150_Vert.jpg")
```

add the appropriate CRS manually:

```{r}
terra::crs(McN_nearmap) <- "epsg:32750"
terra::crs(McN_nm2) <- "epsg:32750"
{strtrim(st_crs(McN_nearmap),30)
strtrim(st_crs(McN_nm2),30)}
```

### Read data

```{r read-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
soils <- read.csv("samples20260618.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
soils <- st_as_sf(soils, coords=c("Longitude","Latitude"), crs=4326, remove=F)
soils <- st_transform(soils, crs=32750)
```

We also make a small sf object of the same spatial extent as the background image:

```{r make-extent, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
McNExtent <- 
  st_as_sf(as.data.frame(matrix(st_bbox(McN_nearmap),nrow=2,ncol=2, byrow=T)), 
           coords=c("V1","V2"), crs=32750)
McNExt2 <- 
  st_as_sf(as.data.frame(matrix(st_bbox(McN_nm2),nrow=2,ncol=2, byrow=T)), 
           coords=c("V1","V2"), crs=32750)
```

Now we can plot our map with some data on it...

```{r McN-nearmap-gg, fig.align='center', fig.width=5.5, fig.height=7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Map of sampling locations at McNess Bridge in June 2026 plotted on a Nearmap spatial raster using functions from the sf, terra, ggplot2, ggspatial, and shadowtext R packages.", results='hold', echo=FALSE}
soils <- read.csv("samples20260618.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
soils <- st_as_sf(soils, coords=c("Longitude","Latitude"), crs=4326, remove=F)
soils <- st_transform(soils, crs=32750)
sourceSoils <- soils[soils$Type=="Source material",]
sourceSoils$ID <- droplevels(sourceSoils$ID)

b0 <- st_bbox(McNExt2)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=McNExt2, col="transparent", fill="transparent") +
  annotation_spatial(data=McN_nm2) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill=ID, shape=ID), data=sourceSoils[1:7,], size=3, stroke=1, 
          color="#FFF")+
  geom_shadowtext(aes(x=st_coordinates(sourceSoils)[1:7,1],
                      y=st_coordinates(sourceSoils)[1:7,2], 
                      label=ID), size=4, fontface=2,
                  data=sourceSoils[1:7,],
                  col="#fff", 
                hjust=c(1,1,0,0,1,0,1),
                nudge_x=(c(1,1,0,0,1,0,1)-0.5)*-6,
                nudge_y=(c(1,0.5,1,0,0,0.5,0.5)-0.5)*4
                ) +
  annotation_scale(text_cex=1.01, text_face=2, text_col="#FFF", width_hint=0.4)+
  annotation_north_arrow(location="tr", 
       style=north_arrow_fancy_orienteering(line_col="#FFF", text_col="#FFF",
                                            text_face="bold")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=adjustcolor(turbo(7),1,.7,.7,.7), guide="none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values=rep(c(21:25), 
                                l=nlevels(sourceSoils$ID)), guide="none")+
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0), limits=c(b0[1], b0[3])) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0), limits=c(b0[2], b0[4])) +
  labs(x="Easting",y="Northing", caption="CRS:UTM Zone 50 south (EPSG:32750). Aerial photograph from nearmap.com") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.key = element_rect(fill="#676"),
        axis.title = element_text(face="bold"),
        legend.text = element_text(size=12),
        legend.title = element_text(size=14, face=2)) +
  coord_sf(datum=32750)
```

## read the data

```{r read-data, paged.print=FALSE, results='hold'}
sed26 <- read.csv("YZsedsAll.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
sed26$Sample.ID <- as.character(sed26$Sample.ID)
sed26$XRD.Sample.ID <- as.character(sed26$XRD.Sample.ID)
# names(sed26)[43] <- "Fe.phases"
# summary(sed26)
(summDF <- data.frame(Variable=colnames(sed26),
                      Has.NA.values=sapply(sed26, function(x){sum(is.na(x))>0}),
                      n.Missing=sapply(sed26, function(x){sum(is.na(x))}),
                      row.names = NULL))
```

## CLR-transform and wrangle

```{r CLR-transformation-and-wrangling, paged.print=FALSE}

noNA <- colnames(sed26)[which(summDF$n.Missing==0)]
numCols <- colnames(sed26)[which(sapply(sed26, is.numeric))]
(keep <- c(colnames(sed26)[1:6],"Flag",intersect(noNA, numCols)))
#check it
cat("Should be the same!\n")
colnames(sed26[,keep])

# make a copy of the relevant columns from the data
s26_clr <- sed26[,keep]
cat("\n\n")
# select just the elements since their names have either 1 or 2 characters
(elements <- colnames(sed26[,keep])[colnames(sed26[,keep]) %in%
                            colnames(sed26)[which(nchar(colnames(sed26))<3)]])
cat("Check that Ca is gone!\n")
# then remove Ca in case of contamination from flocculation after wet-sieving
(elements <- elements[-c(which(elements=="Ca"))])
s26_clr <- s26_clr[,-which(colnames(s26_clr)=="Ca")]

# do CLR transformation to remove compositional closure
s26_clr[,elements] <- 
  t(apply(s26_clr[,elements], MARGIN = 1,
          FUN = function(x){log(x) - mean(log(x), na.rm=T)}))
cat("\n\n")
# check missing value count in numeric columns
sapply(s26_clr[,which(sapply(s26_clr, is.numeric))], function(x){sum(is.na(x))})

# the next code not used yet as we don't have enough XRD data

# s26_clr[,43:46] <- t(apply(sed26[,43:46], MARGIN = 1,
#                           FUN = function(x){log(x) - mean(log(x))}))
# head(s26_clr) # ; summary(s26_clr) ; nrow(s26_clr) ; nrow(na.omit(s26_clr))
# RcmdrMisc::numSummary(s26_clr[,6:ncol(s26_clr)])

# s26_clr$LocType3[grep("Mcness.Sus",s26_clr$LocType3)] <- NA

## Aitchison distances

### Aitchison distances Type centroids

```{r AitDists-centroids, paged.print=FALSE}
n1 <- which(colnames(s26_clr)=="Al");nn <- which(colnames(s26_clr)=="Zn")
TypeCentroids <- data.frame(Type=levels(s26_clr$Type),
                rbind(colMeans(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type=="riparian",n1:nn]),
                      colMeans(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type=="pool",n1:nn]),
                      colMeans(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type=="suspended",n1:nn])))
row.names(TypeCentroids) <- TypeCentroids$Type
(AitDistsType <- dist(TypeCentroids[,-1]))
```

### …and pairwise PERMANOVA…

> Check this using s26_clr2$TypeRip first 🟨⭐🟨⭐🟨⭐🟨⭐🟨

```{r permutest-on-beta-dispersion}
(bd0 <- betadisper(dist(s26_clr2[,n1:nn]), s26_clr2$TypeRip))
permutest(bd0, permutations = 9999)
```

```{r pairwise-permanova, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, paged.print=FALSE}
# used to be done using pairwise.adonis2(), but...
# set it up
pairz <- combn(levels(s26_clr2$TypeRip), 2)
row.names(s26_clr2) <- NULL
row.names(s26_clr2) <- paste0(s26_clr2$TypeRip, row.names(s26_clr2))

# do the pairwise comparisons by normal permanova
pw0 <- apply(pairz,2, FUN=function(pr) {
  keep <- which(s26_clr2$TypeRip %in% pr)
  Dsub <- as.matrix(s26_clr2[keep,n1:nn])
  set.seed(31416)
  a <- adonis2(Dsub ~ s26_clr2$TypeRip[keep], permutations=999, method="euclid")
  c(group1=pr[1], group2=pr[2], Rsq=round(a$R2[1], 3), 
    Fstat=round(a$F[1], 2), p_raw=a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
})
pw0 <- as.data.frame(t(pw0))
pw0[,3:5] <- apply(pw0[,3:5],2,as.numeric)
# colnames(pw0) <- c("group1","group2","Rsq","F","p_raw")

```

Correct pairwise p-values for multiple comparisons (using Holm)

```{r holm-adjust-pw-PERMANOVA, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
# correct for multiple comparisons
pw0$p_holm <- p.adjust(pw0$p_raw, "holm")

grps <- sort(unique(c(pw0$group1, pw0$group2))) # also levels(s26_clr2$TypeRip)

pmat <- matrix(
  NA,
  nrow = length(grps),
  ncol = length(grps),
  dimnames = list(grps, grps)
)

for(i in seq_len(nrow(pw0))) {
  g1 <- pw0$group1[i]
  g2 <- pw0$group2[i]
  pmat[g2, g1] <- pw0$p_holm[i] # just below diag; else pmat[g1,g2]<-pw0$p_holm[i]
}
# show the table!
flextable(data.frame(x1=grps[2:length(grps)],
                     pmat[2:nrow(pmat),1:(ncol(pmat)-1)])) |> 
  set_header_labels(x1="") |> 
  set_caption(caption="Pairwise PERMANOVA p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons using Holm's correction.")
```

```{r print-pairwise-flextable, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
ftpw <- flextable(data.frame(x1=grps[2:length(grps)],
                     pmat[2:nrow(pmat),1:(ncol(pmat)-1)])) |> 
  set_header_labels(x1="") |> 
  set_caption(caption="Pairwise PERMANOVA p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons using Holm's correction.")
htmltools_value(ftpw)
```

     col=mako(nlevels(s26_clr$Type), end=0.7))
```

### Aitchison distances by sample

```{r aitchison-distances, paged.print=FALSE}
row.names(s26_clr) <- s26_clr$Sample.ID
s26_aDists <- dist(s26_clr[,c("Al","Ba","Co","Cr","Cu","Fe","K","La","Mg",
                              "Mn","Na","Ni","P","Pb","S","Sr","V","Y","Zn")], 
                   method="euclidean", diag=TRUE, upper = TRUE)
idx <- row.names(s26_aDists)
cat("Showing the most similar samples to each BOTTOM sediment sample",
    "\nbased on AITCHISON DISTANCES between elemental composition:\n")
for(i in which(s26_clr$Type=="pool")){
  cat("\n",idx[i],"\n",rep("=",nchar(idx[i])),"\n",sep="")
  print(round(head(s26_aDists[order(s26_aDists[,idx[i]]), idx[i]],9),2))
}
```

```{r aitchison-dists-suspended, paged.print=FALSE}
cat("Showing the most similar samples to each SUSPENDED sediment sample",
    "\nbased on AITCHISON DISTANCES between elemental compositions:\n")
for(i in which(s26_clr$Type=="suspended")){
  print(round(head(s26_aDists[order(s26_aDists[,idx[i]]), idx[i]],11),2))
}
```

# LDA on actual compositional variables

### impute any missing values

```{r paged.print=FALSE}
s26.elem <- sed26[, c("Sample.ID", "Loc", "Type","TypeRip", "Depth", "Sieve", 
                      "Al", "Ba", "Ce", "Co", "Cr", "Cu", "Fe", "Gd", "K", "La", 
                      "Mg", "Mn", "Na", "Nd", "Ni", "P", "Pb", "Rb", "S", "Sr", 
                      "Th", "V", "Y", "Zn")] # not "Ca", 
countNAs <- RcmdrMisc::numSummary(s26.elem[,7:30], statistics=c("mean","sd"))$NAs
# K-nearest neighbour imputation for NA values
s26.imp <- impKNNa(s26.elem[,7:30])
# here are the missing value counts:
# Al Ba Ce Co Cr Cu Fe Gd  K La Mg Mn Na Nd Ni  P Pb Rb  S Sr Th  V  Y Zn 
#  0  0  1  0  0  0  0  2  0  0  0  0  0  1  0  0  0  8  0  0  3  0  0  0
```

with(as.data.frame(s26.imp$xImp), plot(Rb ~ K, log="xy", col=2, lwd=3))

       pch=c(15,1), pt.lwd=c(1,3), pt.cex=c(1.2,1), col=c(3,2))
with(as.data.frame(s26.imp$xImp), plot(Nd ~ Al, log="xy", col=2, lwd=3))

       pch=c(15,1), pt.lwd=c(1,3), pt.cex=c(1.2,1), col=c(3,2))
palette("default")
```

### next transform data with isometric log ratios

```{r ilr-transform-and-impute}
ilr0 <- ilr(acomp(s26.elem[,elements[1:which(elements=="Zn")]]))
s26_ilr <- data.frame(s26.elem[,1:6], ilr0)
```

## LDA on ilr-compositions with imputed values

### train with riparian & suspended

```{r}
# train with everything except pool bottom sediments
s26_ilr$LocSieve <- paste0(s26_ilr$Loc, "_", s26_ilr$Sieve)
LDAdata <- droplevels(s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type!="pool",])

# 2. run linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to predict factor level from ILRs
lda0 <- lda(LocSieve ~ V1+V2+V3+V4+V5+V6+V7+V8+V9+V10, 
            data=LDAdata) # for cross-validation include , CV=TRUE
print(lda0)
```

A problem with sub-setting the data like this, *i.e*.:

🤔 train with riparian & suspended, predict pool

🤔 train with riparian, predict suspended & pool

is that re-suspension of pool sediments may also occur in high or turbulent
river flows, meaning pool sediments themselves can also be sources. Therefore an
analysis of similarity may be better than a model to predict categories ??? 🤔

```{r}
lda.pred0 <- predict(lda0, newdata=s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type=="pool",])
predRslt0 <- data.frame(Actual_Sample=s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type=="pool","Sample.ID"],
                        Predicted=
                          colnames(lda.pred0$posterior)[apply(lda.pred0$posterior,1,
                                                              function(x){which(x==max(x))})],
                        round(lda.pred0$post,4),
                        check.names = F)
# predRslt2$correct <- predRslt2$Actual==predRslt2$Predicted
# colnames(predRslt2)[2:5] <- c("Ara.2mm","Ara.63µm","McN.2mm","McN.63µm")
print(predRslt0, row.names=F)
```

## [Dis]Similarity based on Mahalanobis distances in `ilr` compositions

```{r subset-the-groups-for-Mahalanobis, paged.print=FALSE}
# Note: ilr variables are in columns 7:24
riparian <- s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type == "riparian", ]
suspended <- s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type == "suspended", ]
pool <- s26_ilr[s26_ilr$Type == "pool", ]
mu_rip <- colMeans(riparian[,7:24])
S_rip <- cov(riparian[,7:24])
```

### now calculate Mahalanobis distances

```{r calculate-Mahalanobis, paged.print=FALSE}
# 1. pool from riparian
poolFromRiparian <- mahalanobis(pool[,7:24], center=mu_rip, cov=S_rip)
cat("1. Mahalanobis distances of pool bottom sediments from riparian sediments/soils\n")
poolRipDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(poolFromRiparian), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(poolFromRiparian),1))
poolRipDF[order(poolRipDF$MahalDist),]

# 2. suspended from riparian
suspFromRiparian <- mahalanobis(suspended[,7:24], center=mu_rip, cov=S_rip)
cat("\n2. Mahalanobis distances of suspended sediments from riparian sediments/soils\n")
suspRipDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(suspFromRiparian), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(suspFromRiparian),1))
suspRipDF[order(suspRipDF$MahalDist),]

cat("\n\nthis only works when riparian sediments are the reference; for",
    "suspended and pool, there are less observations than variables, so",
    "the covariance matrix is singular")
```

**Note**: comparison of Mahalanobis distances of individual samples with a 
sample category only works when *riparian* sediments are the reference category. 
For suspended and pool, there are less observations than variables, so the 
covariance matrix is singular 👎.

## PCA on `ilr` compositions to reduce variables and avoid singular covariance matrices...

```{r}
PCAilr <- prcomp(s26_ilr[,7:24], scale.=TRUE)

# show variable weightings for first 8 principal components (PCs)
{cat("\nVariable weightings\n")
PCAilr$rot[,1:8] |> round(3)}

# display component variances (eigenvalues)
{cat("...\n\nComponent Variances - CLR-transformed (open) data\n")
  print(round(PCAilr$sdev^2,3))}

# display proportions of variance explained by successive PCs
{cat("...\n\nProportions of variance explained by each component\n")
  round(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2),3)}

# display cumulative proportions of variance explained by PCs
{cat("...\n\nCumulative proportion of variance explained by each component\n")
  cumsum(round(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2),3))}
```

```{r summarise-PCA-eigenvalues, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat("\nThere are",sum(round(PCAilr$sdev^2,3)>1), "principal components with eigenvalues greater than 1.  "); cat("\nThese",sum(round(PCAilr$sdev^2,3)>1), "components together explain", 100*cumsum(round(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2),3))[sum(round(PCAilr$sdev^2,3)>1)], "% of cumulative multiple variance.  ")
varreq <- 0.95
cat("\n\nTo explain ≥ ",varreq*100,"% of multiple variance, ", min(which(cumsum(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2))>varreq)), " principal components are needed.\nThe next component (PC",min(which(cumsum(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2))>varreq))+1,") explains ",round(100*(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2))[min(which(cumsum(PCAilr$sdev^2/sum(PCAilr$sdev^2))>varreq))+1],2),"% of multiple variance.",sep="")
```

### …also check ilr-PC separation

```{r ilr-PCA-biplot, fig.height=6, fig.width=16}
# set up colours and graphics parameters

# plot standard PCA biplot but hiding observation scores ("transparent")

mtext(paste0("Scaled PC",v2," Observation Scores"), 4, 1.4, font = 2)

# add observation scores to plot; different symbols/colours by `TypeRip` factor
points(PCAilr$x[,v1]*sf, PCAilr$x[,v2]*sf*1.5,

# SECOND BIPLOT --------------------------------------------------------

biplot(PCAilr, choices = c(v1,v2), col = c("transparent","#888"), cex=c(.9,1.1)*sf,
       pc.biplot = FALSE, arrow.len = 0.08, cex.lab=1.2*sf, scale=1, 
       # change xlim, ylim if needed, to show all data
       xlim = c(-0.6,0.6), ylim = c(-0.6,0.6),

points(PCAilr$x[,v1]*sf, PCAilr$x[,v2]*sf*1.5,

### what elements do ilr-PCs represent?

```{r correl-clr-elements-with-ilr-PCs, paged.print=FALSE}
corElemPC <- cor(cbind(s26_clr[,elements],PCAilr$x[,1:9]))
corDF <- data.frame(
  PC1elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC1"]),"PC1"]),
  PC1r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC1"]),"PC1"],3),
  PC2elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC2"]),"PC2"]),
  PC2r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC2"]),"PC2"],3),
  PC3elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC3"]),"PC3"]),
  PC3r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC3"]),"PC3"],3),
  PC4elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC4"]),"PC4"]),
  PC4r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC4"]),"PC4"],3),
  PC5elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC5"]),"PC5"]),
  PC5r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC5"]),"PC5"],3),
  PC6elem=names(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC6"]),"PC6"]),
  PC6r=round(corElemPC[order(corElemPC[,"PC6"]),"PC6"],3)
)
print(corDF, row.names=F)
cat("\nNote that the PCs should not be correlated with one another, i.e. we see all PC*r ≃ 0.")
```

### Now do Mahalanobis distances based on the ilr-PCs

```{r Mahalanobis-from-ilr-PCs}
MahalData <- data.frame(Sample=s26_ilr$Sample.ID, Type=s26_ilr$Type, 
                        PCAilr$x[,1:9])


# Note: ilr variables are in columns 7:24
riparian <- MahalData[MahalData$Type == "riparian", ]
suspended <- MahalData[MahalData$Type == "suspended", ]
pool <- MahalData[MahalData$Type == "pool", ]
mu_rip <- colMeans(riparian[,3:11])
S_rip <- cov(riparian[,3:11])
mu_susp <- colMeans(suspended[,3:11])
S_susp <- cov(suspended[,3:11])
mu_pool <- colMeans(pool[,3:11])
S_pool <- cov(pool[,3:11])
```

### now calculate Mahalanobis distances

```{r calculate-Mahalanobis, paged.print=FALSE}
# 1. pool from riparian
poolFromRiparian <- mahalanobis(pool[,3:11], center=mu_rip, cov=S_rip)
cat("1. Mahalanobis distances of pool bottom sediments FROM RIPARIAN SOILS\n")
poolRipDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(poolFromRiparian), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(poolFromRiparian),1))
poolRipDF[order(poolRipDF$MahalDist),]

# 2. suspended from riparian
suspFromRiparian <- mahalanobis(suspended[,3:11], center=mu_rip, cov=S_rip)
cat("\n2. Mahalanobis distances of suspended sediments FROM RIPARIAN SOILS\n")
suspRipDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(suspFromRiparian), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(suspFromRiparian),1))
suspRipDF[order(suspRipDF$MahalDist),]

# 3. pool from suspended
poolFromSusp <- mahalanobis(pool[,3:11], center=mu_susp, cov=S_susp)
cat("\n3. Mahalanobis distances of pool bottom sediments FROM SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS\n")
poolSuspDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(poolFromSusp), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(poolFromSusp),1))
poolSuspDF[order(poolSuspDF$MahalDist),]

# 4. riparian from suspended
riparianFromSusp <- mahalanobis(riparian[,3:11], center=mu_susp, cov=S_susp)
cat("\n4. Mahalanobis distances of riparian soils FROM SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS\n")
riparianSuspDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(riparianFromSusp), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(riparianFromSusp),1))
riparianSuspDF[order(riparianSuspDF$MahalDist),]

# 5. suspended from pool
suspFromPool <- mahalanobis(suspended[,3:11], center=mu_pool, cov=S_pool)
cat("\n5. Mahalanobis distances of pool bottom sediments FROM SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS\n")
suspPoolDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(suspFromPool), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(suspFromPool),1))
suspPoolDF[order(suspPoolDF$MahalDist),]

# 6. riparian from pool
riparianFromPool <- mahalanobis(riparian[,3:11], center=mu_pool, cov=S_pool)
cat("\n6. Mahalanobis distances of riparian soils FROM SUSPENDED SEDIMENTS\n")
riparianPoolDF <- data.frame(Sample=names(riparianFromPool), 
                        MahalDist=round(unname(riparianFromPool),1))
riparianPoolDF[order(riparianPoolDF$MahalDist),]
```

# Linear Discriminant Analysis Prediction

## 1. Train with everything except pool bottom (core) sediments

```{r do-initial-LDA-predict-train-with-sources, paged.print=FALSE}
# 1. add PCs to data frame 
s26_clr <- cbind(s26_clr, pca2$x[,1:12])

# train with everything except pool bottom sediments
LDAdata <- droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type!="pool",])

# 2. run linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to predict factor level from PCs
lda1 <- lda(LocSieve ~ PC1+PC2+PC3+PC4+PC5+PC6+PC7+PC8+PC9+PC10, 
            data=LDAdata) # for cross-validation include , CV=TRUE
print(lda1)

# show LDA predictions
cat("\n\nLDA self-predictions\n====================\n")
lda1.pred <- predict(lda1) # won't work if CV=TRUE is included in lda(...)
predRslt <- data.frame(Actual=LDAdata$LocSieve,round(lda1.pred$post,3),
                       Predicted=colnames(lda1.pred$posterior)[apply(lda1.pred$posterior,1,
                                                                     function(x){which(x==max(x))})],
                       check.names = F)
predRslt$correct <- predRslt$Actual==predRslt$Predicted
# colnames(predRslt)[2:5] <- c("Ara.2mm","Ara.63µm","McN.2mm","McN.63µm")
print(predRslt, row.names=F)
```

### 1.1 Predict where pool bottom sediments might have come from...

```{r}
lda.pred2 <- predict(lda1, newdata=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type=="pool",])
predRslt2 <- data.frame(Actual_Sample=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type=="pool","Sample.ID"],
                       Predicted=colnames(lda.pred2$posterior)[apply(lda.pred2$posterior,1,
                                                                     function(x){which(x==max(x))})],
                        round(lda.pred2$post,4),
                       check.names = F)
# predRslt2$correct <- predRslt2$Actual==predRslt2$Predicted
# colnames(predRslt2)[2:5] <- c("Ara.2mm","Ara.63µm","McN.2mm","McN.63µm")
print(predRslt2, row.names=F)
```

## 2. Train with only terrestrial sediments (car park, firebreaks, riparian soil)

```{r do-initial-LDA-predict-train-with-erosional, paged.print=FALSE}

# 2. run linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to predict factor level from PCs
lda1 <- lda(LocSieve ~ PC1+PC2+PC3+PC4+PC5+PC6+PC7+PC8+PC9+PC10, 
            data=LDAdata) # for cross-validation include , CV=TRUE
print(lda1)

# show LDA predictions
cat("\n\nLDA predictions\n===============\n")
lda1.pred <- predict(lda1) # won't work if CV=TRUE is included in lda(...)
predRslt <- data.frame(Actual=LDAdata$LocSieve,round(lda1.pred$post,4),
                       Predicted=colnames(lda1.pred$posterior)[apply(lda1.pred$posterior,1,
                                                                     function(x){which(x==max(x))})],
                       check.names = F)
predRslt$correct <- predRslt$Actual==predRslt$Predicted
# colnames(predRslt)[2:5] <- c("Ara.2mm","Ara.63µm","McN.2mm","McN.63µm")
print(predRslt, row.names=F)

# 4. Support Vector Machine (SVM) Prediction

## 4.1 Train SVM with just erosional samples

```{r support-vector-machine}
sv1 <- svm(LocSieve ~ ., 
                data=droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", c("LocSieve", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5", 
                           "PC6", "PC7", "PC8", "PC9", "PC10", "PC11", "PC12")]), 
        ## TUNING PARAMETERS
        cost=2,     # default = 1
        gamma=0.05, # default is 1/(number of predictors) # 1/12 = 0.083
        # degree=3, # only for polynomial kernel # see help for others
        # leave this one 👇
        kernel="radial" # kernel can be "linear" or "polynomial"
        )
# str(sv1)
print(sv1)
sv1pred <- predict(sv1, s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", 
                                c("LocSieve", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5", 
                           "PC6", "PC7", "PC8", "PC9", "PC10", "PC11", "PC12")])
cat("\nTraining-Predictions from Support Vector Machine\n",rep("=",48),"\n",sep="")
print(data.frame(Actual=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", "LocSieve"], 
                 Predicted=sv1pred, 
                 Correct=(droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", "LocSieve"])==sv1pred)))
```

## 4.2 Predictions of Unknowns using a Support Vector Machine

```{r predict-susp-bottom-from-svm-trained-with-sources, paged.print=FALSE}
title <- "Predictions of Unknowns using a Support Vector Machine"
sv1predUnknowns <-
  predict(sv1, decision.values = TRUE, 
          newdata = s26_clr[s26_clr$Type != "riparian", 
                            c("LocSieve", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5", 
                           "PC6", "PC7", "PC8", "PC9", "PC10", "PC11", "PC12")])
DV1predUnknowns <-as.data.frame(attr(sv1predUnknowns, "decision.values"))
  colnames(DV1predUnknowns) <- gsub("McNess","Mc",colnames(DV1predUnknowns))
  colnames(DV1predUnknowns) <- gsub("Araluen","Ar",colnames(DV1predUnknowns))
  colnames(DV1predUnknowns) <- gsub("Canning","Can",colnames(DV1predUnknowns))
  colnames(DV1predUnknowns) <- gsub("um","",colnames(DV1predUnknowns))
  colnames(DV1predUnknowns) <- gsub("mm","",colnames(DV1predUnknowns))
cat(title,"\n",rep("=",nchar(title)),"\n",sep="")
print(data.frame(Sample=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type != "riparian", "LocSieve"],
                 Depth=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type != "riparian", "Depth"],
                 Type=s26_clr[s26_clr$Type != "riparian", "Type"], 
        Predicted_source=sv1predUnknowns))
```

# Gradient Boosting Prediction

A gradient-boosted _tree_ classifier is the only option for classifying 
non-numeric categories.

```{r gradient-boosting-tree}
gbTree1 <- xgboost(x=droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", c("LocSieve", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5", 
                           "PC6", "PC7", "PC8", "PC9", "PC10", "PC11", "PC12")]),
               y=droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", "LocSieve"]), 
        ## TUNING PARAMETERS
        objective = "multi:softprob", # ... default for factor with >2 levels
        eval_metric = "logloss",          # default "logloss" for classification
        nrounds = 100L,               # default 100 (L means integer)
        max_depth = 6,                # default 6
        learning_rate = 0.3,          # default 0.3 for tree booster
        reg_lambda = 1,               # default 1 for tree booster
        booster="gbtree"
        )
# str(gbTree1)
# print(gbTree1)
gbTree1pred <- predict(gbTree1, droplevels(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", c("LocSieve", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5", 
                           "PC6", "PC7", "PC8", "PC9", "PC10", "PC11", "PC12")]))
cat("\nPredictions from Gradient boosting (linear)\n",rep("=",43),"\n",sep="")
gbTree1summ <- data.frame(Actual=as.vector(s26_clr[s26_clr$Type == "riparian", "LocSieve"]), 
                 Predicted=colnames(gbTree1pred)[unname(unlist(lapply(apply(gbTree1pred, 1, 
             FUN=function(x){which(x==max(x, na.rm=T))}), function(x){head(x,1)})))])
gbTree1summ$Correct <- gbTree1summ$Actual == gbTree1summ$Predicted
print(gbTree1summ)
```
